A scientist's broad optical influence should not all be attributed to the specific negative-index discovery. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/bio/sir-john-pendry))

### 11. Quantum cascade lasers

The original paper was published **April 22, 1994**, and demonstrated a fundamentally different semiconductor laser based on sequential electronic transitions. A **December 4, 2024** retrospective coauthored by Faist describes its evolution into a major coherent mid-infrared and terahertz source. This is a mature, practically important and discrete invention. Its lower probability is comparative: I found less fresh selection-relevant recognition for this particular invention than for clocks, twistronics or several other listed discoveries. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17732739/?utm_source=openai))

### 12. Cosmic inflation

Inflation has immense theoretical importance, but my primary concern is empirical closure. A **June 11, 2026** BICEP collaboration proceedings paper still discusses forthcoming constraints and instrumental-systematics control, rather than announcing a decisive inflationary-gravitational-wave detection. A date-bounded arXiv search through the cutoff did not establish a new confirmation that would materially change this assessment. That search is not proof that no relevant result exists, and a Nobel need not require tensor-mode detection; nevertheless, I judge this option substantially less likely than the experimentally settled alternatives. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13942))

## Why Other remains large

The named list is broad, but it is not an official or exhaustive scientific shortlist. Important omitted possibilities include **photonic crystals/band gaps**, for which Berkeley identifies Yablonovitch's foundational role, and **exoplanet characterization and atmospheres**, recognized by the **2024 Kavli Astrophysics Prize** to Charbonneau and Seager. These are separate discovery narratives, even where scientists or neighboring fields overlap the options. ([www2.eecs.berkeley.edu](https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Homepages/yablonovitch.html))

There is also fresh evidence of omitted candidates. Clarivate's release dated **September 17, 2026** recognized advanced organic light-emitting diodes, magnetoelectric multiferroics and the experimental quantum anomalous Hall effect. I use this as a modest reminder of the breadth of Nobel-class work, not as a same-year Nobel prediction. A standalone anomalous-Hall discovery would likely be Other, whereas a motivation centered on the broader topological-insulator discovery could match the first option; I retain uncertainty around that boundary. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/?utm_source=openai))

Other therefore represents an aggregate of credible omitted discoveries plus unexpected choices and discovery-boundary uncertainty. It does **not** mean that any one omitted discovery has a 31.8% chance.

## Historical base rates and treatment of the supplied profiles

I retrieved the official Physics award series for **2000–2025 inclusive: 26 annual prize observations**, with announcement dates from **October 10, 2000, through October 7, 2025**. The vintage is the official historical record available at the forecast cutoff. My own coarse, mutually exclusive classification gives: AMO/optics/quantum information **7/26**; condensed matter **4/26**; astrophysics/cosmology **6/26**; particle physics **4/26**; electronic/optoelectronic technology **3/26**; complex/interdisciplinary systems **2/26**. I classify 2025 circuits in the broad quantum group and use one category per prize year, not one per laureate. These are analyst-defined categories, not Nobel classifications. The historical diversity—including climate/complexity and neural-network foundations—supports a meaningful residual rather than confidence in a familiar candidate list. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-prizes-in-physics/all/?gallery_style=page&utm_source=openai))

I did not infer a deterministic field rotation or that astronomy is now due. The sample is small, discoveries span categories, and historical waiting times are difficult to define consistently. History supplies a breadth check, not a fitted discovery-specific probability.

The client-supplied bibliometrics were used only as qualitative context. They compare selected candidates with winners, without a denominator of unsuccessful Nobel-ready discoveries; they mix career-wide measures with prize-time records; and they are person-level rather than discovery-level. There are also apparent metadata problems, notably the supplied Bennett publication window beginning in **1857**. These could materially distort a numerical ranking. The official 2000–2025 list contains **71 named laureates**, so the supplied 62-person reference group is not the complete cohort unless it incorporates an additional missing-data or eligibility filter. I did not assume those profile percentiles are calibrated winning probabilities. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-prizes-in-physics/all/?gallery_style=page&utm_source=openai))

## Numerical construction

I used a transparent **judgmental ensemble**, not a trained statistical model. Its components share evidence and should not be mistaken for independent studies.

### A. Bottom-up discovery model

Before the fresh precursor adjustments, I allocated **0.30 to Other** and **0.70 across the named discoveries**, using the following relative weights. The weights incorporate scientific maturity, significance, Nobel-style discovery fit, overlap and wording concerns discussed above. They are elicited comparative judgments, not citation-derived odds.

| Discovery | Base weight w | Fresh-evidence multiplier m |
|---|---:|---:|
| Topological insulators/QSH | 90 | 1.00 |
| Optical lattice clocks | 110 | 1.08 |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 32 | 1.00 |
| Geometric phases | 40 | 1.00 |
| Magic-angle graphene | 40 | 1.25 |
| Foundational quantum information | 50 | 1.00 |
| High-energy cosmic neutrinos | 36 | 1.00 |
| Black-hole shadow/EHT | 30 | 1.00 |
| Optical-lattice simulators | 60 | 1.08 |
| Quantum cascade laser | 24 | 1.00 |
| Aberration-corrected electron optics | 45 | 1.00 |
| Cosmic inflation | 6 | 1.00 |
| Other | Separate 0.30 allocation | 1.10 |

The named weights sum to **563**. Thus the initial named probabilities are **a_i = 0.70 × w_i / 563**, with **a_Other = 0.30**. Apply the multipliers and normalize: **B_i = a_i × m_i / Z**, where **Z = 1.0593428063943162**. The small clock/simulator multipliers reflect the cautiously treated Wolf evidence; the graphene multiplier reflects the June Kavli recognition; the Other multiplier reflects fresh recognition of omitted possibilities. These are conservative judgmental updates, not measured likelihood ratios.

### B. Broad-field model

To reduce anchoring on the named list, I independently structured the allocation by field, informed—but not mechanically determined—by the historical counts:

- **Quantum/AMO: 0.27**, divided conditionally into clocks 0.47, lattice simulation 0.28, foundational quantum information 0.20, Other 0.05.
- **Condensed matter/topological foundations: 0.22**, divided into topological insulators 0.46, geometric phases 0.20, magic-angle graphene 0.20, Other 0.14.
- **Astrophysics/particle physics: 0.33**, divided into high-energy neutrinos 0.18, EHT 0.16, inflation 0.02, Other 0.64.
- **Other instrumental/device physics: 0.13**, divided into metamaterials 0.23, corrected electron optics 0.35, quantum cascade lasers 0.20, Other 0.22.
- **Unlisted/interdisciplinary discoveries: 0.05**, entirely Other.

Multiplying each field probability by its conditional allocations gives model **F**, including **F_Other = 0.3341**. The field probabilities and conditional allocations are explicitly subjective current-pool judgments; the historical sample does not statistically identify them.

### C. Combination, precision and uncertainty

The final calculation is **P_i = 0.70 × B_i + 0.30 × F_i**. I performed normalization and sensitivity calculations in Python. Each output is rounded to six decimal places, with the **0.000001 rounding residual assigned to Other**, making the reported probabilities sum exactly to 1.000000.

As an elicitation sensitivity check, I multiplied the updated bottom-up Other weight by **0.8, 1.0 or 1.3**, and the clock weight by **0.7, 1.0 or 1.4**, renormalized, and retained the same ensemble blend. Across those nine cases, clocks range from approximately **10.3% to 17.6%**, and Other from **27.6% to 37.0%**. These are sensitivity ranges, **not statistical confidence intervals**, and broader misspecification could produce larger changes.

The six-decimal outputs preserve the reproducible arithmetic; they do not imply that Nobel selection is known to six-decimal accuracy. The strongest conclusions are the substantial Other allocation, clocks and topological insulators leading the named candidates, and inflation receiving a much lower probability because of its comparatively unresolved empirical case.

## TL;DR

Other is the leading resolution category at 32.3%. Optical lattice clocks lead the named discoveries at 15%, followed by topological insulators at 10% and negative-index metamaterials at 8%. Keep the forecast dispersed: no named discovery has a dominant probability.

## Context

This forecast uses the client’s information cutoff of October 1, 2026, at 23:43 UTC. The official Physics announcement is scheduled for October 6, 2026, at 11:45 CEST at the earliest, equivalent to 09:45 UTC. The announcement remains the future resolving event; earlier discoveries and scientific awards are evidence, not resolutions ([official schedule](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/)).

The committee’s recommendations are prepared before the announcement, but the Academy makes the final choice in early October. Nominations and evaluations remain confidential for 50 years. That leaves public scientific recognition, experimental maturity, and institutional attention as useful but indirect evidence. The three-person limit affects how easily credit can be allocated; it does not require the names in an option to match the eventual laureates ([selection process](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/); [Nobel statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/)).

## Evidence

The historical backbone is the complete record of 26 annual Physics prizes from October 10, 2000, through October 7, 2025, using completed award records available at the cutoff. The observation unit is a prize-year, not a laureate. My classification finds nine prizes, or 34.6%, divided between different motivations. That makes the client’s discovery-share rule consequential, but does not establish a historical winning rate for this particular shortlist ([official award record](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-prizes-in-physics/)).

| Prize year | Recognized subjects, abbreviated |

| [2006](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2006/summary/) | Cosmic microwave background |

| [2025](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2025/summary/) | Quantum tunnelling and quantisation in circuits |

This history supports breadth, not a reliable field-rotation rule. I apply modest discounts for overlap with earlier prizes rather than assuming that a field is either exhausted or due. I also give the supplied bibliometrics no numerical selection weight. Comparisons with previous winners lack the nonwinner population needed to estimate winning odds, and career-wide prominence is not the same as recognition of a particular discovery.

Optical lattice clocks have the strongest compact invention-and-experiment case. The 2022 Breakthrough Prize, announced on September 9, 2021, explicitly recognized Katori and Ye for this discovery. RIKEN’s May 12, 2026 agreement with BIPM and Shimadzu adds evidence of practical and standards relevance ([Breakthrough citation](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/65); [RIKEN agreement](https://www.riken.jp/en/news_pubs/news/2026/20260512_2/index.html)). The second has not already been redefined: BIPM still describes a future optical-frequency proposal for the 2030 conference. I read that as evidence of consequence, not a prerequisite that the Nobel must wait to satisfy. Nor do all optical-clock advances support this precise option: NIST’s July 14, 2025 accuracy-record announcement concerned an aluminium-ion clock ([BIPM roadmap](https://www.bipm.org/en/time-department/time-future); [NIST announcement](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/07/nist-ion-clock-sets-new-record-most-accurate-clock-world)).

Metamaterials have the most interesting institutional weak signal. Umeå’s June 29, 2026 announcement said the entire Physics Nobel Committee would attend its June 29–July 1 symposium, whose speakers included Pendry and Smith. Wilczek’s subsequent participant account says the committee attended. Pendry’s 2024 Kyoto citation independently establishes the maturity of the negative-index theory-to-experiment story ([Umeå announcement](https://www.umu.se/en/news/top-physicists-gather-for-nobel-symposium-at-umea-university_12180282/); [participant account](https://www.frankawilczek.com/single-post/frank-wilczek-at-the-2026-nobel-symposium-in-physics); [Kyoto citation](https://www.kyotoprize.org/en/laureates/john_pendry/)).

The symposium deserves an update, not a leap to overwhelming favoritism. The complete Academy catalogue for 2000–2025 contains 22 Physics-labelled meetings and two additional mixed-field meetings. My coding identifies two narrow, pre-announcement same-year matches—graphene and attoseconds—and two broader matches—LHC/Higgs and emerging quantum technologies. Many other themes did not produce a matching near-term prize. These events are clustered, their scopes differ, and historical committee attendance is not systematically recorded ([complete symposium catalogue](https://www.kva.se/en/research-funding/nobel-symposia/nobel-symposia-previous/)). The metamaterials meeting was already publicly announced on November 11, 2025, so its topic was not a last-minute revelation of committee preference ([advance announcement](https://www.umu.se/en/news/two-nobel-symposia-at-umea-university-in-2026_12148986/)).

Topological insulators retain a strong theory–experiment narrative. Kane’s selection for the 2026 Lorentz Medal, announced on September 4, 2025, adds discovery-specific endorsement. The main discount is adjacency to the earlier topology Nobel, not scientific weakness ([Penn announcement](https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/penn-physicist-charles-kane-receive-2026-lorentz-medal); [2016 Nobel motivation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2016/summary/)). Magic-angle graphene gains from the 2026 Kavli Nanoscience citation, which connects the theoretical framework with correlated insulating states and superconductivity. Its shorter consolidation period keeps it below the leading mature candidates; the different Kavli recipient list is not a resolution penalty ([Kavli citation](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/nanoscience/2026)).

Quantum-information foundations and optical-lattice simulation both remain credible. ACM’s March 18, 2026 announcement of Bennett and Brassard’s 2025 Turing Award strengthens the first category. The August 5, 2025 announcement of the Micius Prize specifically for optical-lattice quantum simulation supports the second ([ACM announcement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/acm-am-turing-award-honors-charles-h-bennett-and-gilles-brassard-for-foundational-contributions-to-quantum-information-science-302716290.html); [Max Planck announcement](https://www.mpq.mpg.de/7090982/08-micius-quantum-prize-for-immanuel-bloch)). The other scheduled Physics Nobel Symposium is less useful as evidence of completed committee exposure: the quantum-computing meeting runs October 25–30, 2026, after the prize announcement, and covers a broader subject than neutral-atom simulation ([meeting schedule](https://www.nqcc.ac.uk/events/nobel-symposium-in-physics-quantum-computing/)).

Geometric phases and aberration-corrected electron optics have mature foundational cases. The joint 2026 Wigner recognition of Berry and Aharonov adds a modest current signal; the 2020 Kavli citation establishes the electron-optics breakthrough independently of its relatively modest supplied citation metrics. The quantum cascade laser also has a clear, long-established invention narrative, documented in an inventor-authored retrospective ([Wigner award](https://wignermedal.tamu.edu/); [electron-optics citation](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/nanoscience/2020); [laser retrospective](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42005-024-01888-z)).

The astronomical candidates open genuine observational windows, but distributed credit makes individual allocation harder. IceCube’s November 21, 2013 discovery announcement concerned observations collected from May 2010 through May 2012. EHT’s April 10, 2019 announcement reported black-hole-shadow imaging through an international telescope collaboration ([IceCube discovery](https://icecube.wisc.edu/news/press-releases/2013/11/icecube-pushes-neutrinos-to-forefront-of-astronomy/); [EHT discovery](https://eventhorizontelescope.org/press-release-april-10-2019-astronomers-capture-first-image-black-hole)). I rank these below the leading inventions. Inflation ranks lowest because I found no verified new observation that changes its confirmation case; the BICEP status report revised August 27, 2026 still describes its next analysis as forthcoming ([BICEP report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25015v2)).

Other is a substantive competing pool. Clarivate’s September 17, 2026 recognition identifies efficient OLEDs, magnetoelectric multiferroics, and quantum anomalous Hall research. The 2026 Kavli Astrophysics citation adds Galactic assembly, another omitted discovery family. These establish credible omissions, not knowledge of this year’s Nobel shortlist ([Clarivate announcement](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/); [Physics citations](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physics/); [Kavli Astrophysics citation](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2026)).

I translated this evidence into the following judgmental weights. The starting weights encode maturity, experimental support, distinctness, attribution, and prior-prize overlap. The adjustments reflect the checked recognition signals and omitted pool. They are not fitted likelihood ratios or observed frequencies.

| Discovery | Starting weight | Adjustment | Resolution weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Topological insulators | 13 | 1.00 | 13.00 |
| Optical lattice clocks | 16 | 1.20 | 19.20 |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 6 | 2.00, then matching allowance | 10.20 |
| Geometric phases | 5 | 1.20 | 6.00 |
| Magic-angle graphene | 7 | 1.20 | 8.40 |
| Quantum-information foundations | 6 | 1.10 | 6.60 |
| Cosmic neutrinos | 4 | 1.00 | 4.00 |
| Black-hole shadow | 3 | 1.00 | 3.00 |
| Optical-lattice simulation | 6 | 1.10 | 6.60 |
| Quantum cascade laser | 4 | 1.00 | 4.00 |
| Aberration-corrected electron optics | 6 | 1.00 | 6.00 |
| Inflation | 1 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Other | 23 | 1.75, plus unmatched weight | 42.05 |

The metamaterials update initially produces 12 weight units. I allocate 15% of that updated family weight to Other because a prize centred on a distinct metasurface or photonic-crystal discovery would not automatically match negative-index materials. This transfers 1.80 units without changing the total. Each final probability is its resolution weight divided by 130.05. The additional decimal places in the probability object preserve this arithmetic; they do not measure committee uncertainty to that precision.

## What's non-obvious

**Harald Rose’s death does not justify collapsing the electron-optics discovery’s probability.** His death on July 27, 2026 is confirmed, and he cannot receive a posthumous Nobel under the normal rule. But that changes recipient eligibility, not the eligibility of surviving contributors’ achievements. The three-person ceiling can even make the remaining allocation simpler, although that is an inference, not evidence of committee intent ([institutional obituary](https://www.iap.tu-darmstadt.de/angewandte_physik/iap_news_details_125312.de.jsp); [statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/)). A relevant counterexample is LIGO: co-founder Ronald Drever died on March 7, 2017, and the discovery still received that year’s Physics prize. This does not prove that a recent death helps, but it argues against an assumed institutional prohibition or overwhelming awkwardness penalty ([Caltech obituary](https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-mourns-passing-ligo-co-founder-ronald-w-drever-54336); [2017 award](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2017/summary/)).

Discovery matching matters more than matching names. A broad metamaterials citation can match when the negative-index invention is central; a photonic-crystal-only citation cannot be forced into that option because of a shared scientist. Likewise, I classify a narrowly quantum-anomalous-Hall award as Other, while allowing a broader topological-insulator motivation to match the listed category. The original anomalous-Hall experiment explicitly concerns magnetic topological insulators, which explains both the relationship and the classification risk ([original experiment](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23493424/)).

## Uncertainties

The largest missing evidence is the confidential evaluation and final recommendation. Public honours are correlated endorsements of scientific standing, not independent observations of Nobel votes. A complete historical record of symposium attendance, actual meeting dates, and comparable ordinary conferences would sharpen the institutional-attention update. Without that denominator, I keep it moderate rather than presenting a fitted predictive effect ([selection confidentiality](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/); [symposium archive](https://www.kva.se/en/research-funding/nobel-symposia/nobel-symposia-previous/)).

The largest numerical uncertainty is shortlist coverage, followed by the weight assigned to clocks and metamaterials. In joint stress tests varying those three adjustments, Other ranges from 25% to 40.4%, clocks from 10% to 20%, and negative-index metamaterials from 5% to 13%. These are model-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals. The final motivation and the larger-share/first-listed rule can also move outcomes across discovery boundaries, so the forecast retains a substantial unlisted tail.
subforecast_write_ups:
## Forecast summary

**Top named outcome: negative-index metamaterials (16.5%).** Optical lattice clocks rank second at 12.5%, followed by magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene at 7.5%. I retain **29.7% for Other**, because several credible discoveries are absent from the named options and Nobel Physics choices are frequently surprising.

This forecast uses information available through **October 1, 2026 at 23:32 UTC**. The official announcement is scheduled for **October 6, 2026 at 11:45 CEST at the earliest**. Nominations and evaluations are confidential for 50 years; nominations closed January 31, external evaluation occurred during March–May, the committee report was prepared in June–August, and recommendations went to the Academy in September. Consequently, there is no reliable public shortlist or nomination count to use. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/?utm_source=openai))

I did **not** use prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public forecast aggregates.

## Method

I combined three approaches:

1. **Historical/base-rate model.** I collected the 25 annual Physics prizes from 2001–2025 from official Nobel data and classified each by broad field. The most recent ten included three astrophysics/cosmology prizes, two atomic/optical prizes, two quantum-information or quantum-circuit prizes, two condensed-matter prizes, and one interdisciplinary/other prize. Field rotation was assigned only modest weight because adjacent areas often win close together.
2. **Discovery-lag and attribution model.** I scored maturity, experimental confirmation, precursor prizes, whether credit can be allocated to at most three living people, overlap with recent Nobels, and whether the likely official motivation would match the option wording. A selected sample of 11 recent discoveries had award lags ranging from 2 to 55 years, with a median near 33 years; this was not a random sample and therefore was used as a soft prior, not a fitted frequency law.
3. **Weak-signal overlay.** I looked for current precursor prizes, changes in committee expertise, Swedish institutional activity, deaths, and unusual attention from Nobel-linked institutions. This changed the rankings, especially for metamaterials, magic-angle graphene, geometric phases, and aberration-corrected microscopy.

The official 2026 committee contains expertise in astroparticle physics, theoretical magnetism, atomic physics, quantum physics, complex systems, and microscopy. This makes several options legible to the committee, but committee specialties are a weak signal because outside experts are used and members serve multi-year terms. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/about/the-nobel-committee-for-physics?utm_source=openai))

The user-provided bibliometric profiles were treated as secondary evidence. They establish that nearly every listed group is scientifically distinguished, but are not very discriminating: publication and patent totals do not reveal nominations, resolve contested credit, or indicate which field the Academy wants to recognize this year.

## The most important weak signal: the 2026 Nobel Symposium on metamaterials

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences lists two Physics Nobel Symposia in 2026: **“Metamaterials science and technology: structuring light and sound in space and time”** and **“Quantum Computing and Simulation.”** ([kva.se](https://www.kva.se/en/research-funding/nobel-symposia/))

The metamaterials symposium occurred in Umeå on **June 29–July 1, 2026**, during the period in which the Nobel Committee normally writes its report. A participant account says the entire Physics Nobel Committee attended as observers. Its invited speakers included **John Pendry, David Smith, and Federico Capasso**, alongside other leading metamaterials researchers. ([frankawilczek.com](https://www.frankawilczek.com/single-post/frank-wilczek-at-the-2026-nobel-symposium-in-physics))

This is not a leak and symposium topics are proposed through a separate academic process. Nevertheless, Nobel Symposia have sometimes preceded or coincided with related prizes: “Graphene and Quantum Matter” was held in 2010, “Large Hadron Collider” in 2013, “New forms of Matter – Topological Insulators and Superconductors” in 2014, “Emerging quantum technologies” in 2022, “Attosecond Science and Technology” in 2023, and “Quantum control of mechanical systems” in 2024. The corresponding Nobel topics appeared in 2010, 2013, 2016, 2022, 2023, and—in a looser thematic sense—2025. There are also numerous false positives, including dark matter and anyons, so this is a meaningful but highly noisy indicator. ([kva.se](https://www.kva.se/en/research-funding/nobel-symposia/nobel-symposia-previous/?utm_source=openai))

Pendry also received the **2024 Kyoto Prize** for establishing the theoretical framework by which engineered structures can produce properties such as negative refractive index; the Kyoto citation explicitly notes the subsequent first experimental demonstration. This combination of scientific maturity, recent high-level recognition, and unusually direct 2026 Nobel-linked attention is why metamaterials lead my forecast. ([kyotoprize.org](https://www.kyotoprize.org/en/laureates/john_pendry/))

I stop at 16.5%, rather than making metamaterials an overwhelming favorite, because attribution is not completely clean. Pendry and Smith are central to negative-index metamaterials, but the appropriate third laureate could be Capasso, Andrea Alù, Nader Engheta, or another researcher rather than Eli Yablonovitch. The resolution criteria mitigate the personnel mismatch, but a broader motivation centered on metasurfaces, transformation optics, or another aspect of engineered wave materials could create matching ambiguity.

## Optical lattice clocks: 12.5%

Optical lattice clocks have perhaps the cleanest Nobel-shaped attribution among the options. Katori and Ye divided the 2022 Breakthrough Prize for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock; NIST describes the work as enabling precision tests of fundamental laws and identifies Katori as receiving the other half of Ye’s prize. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2021/09/nistjila-fellow-jun-ye-wins-breakthrough-prize-fundamental-physics))

The selection process is unusually opaque. Nobel's published procedure has nominations closing on January 31, expert consultation during March–May, preparation of recommendations during June–August, discussion during September, and the Academy's final selection in early October. Nomination and deliberation information is confidential for 50 years. Consequently, public scientific recognition is useful evidence of award-readiness, but it is not evidence that a discovery is on the committee's actual final shortlist. 3. **Shortlist coverage and resolution matching:** Which credible discoveries are omitted, and when might an award involving a listed scientist nevertheless resolve to Other?

No prediction-market prices, betting odds, or community probability aggregates were used. I also commissioned a specialist assessment. ## 5. Numerical construction

There is no defensible public dataset of current eligible discoveries and committee preferences from which to fit a calibrated Nobel-selection model. I therefore use an explicit **judgmental prior-and-update calculation**, not an empirical regression or purported measured Bayes factors.

The starting probabilities below reflect maturity, distinctness, experimental support, attribution, and prior Nobel overlap before the discovery-specific current-recognition updates. Other is a composite category and is not assigned the same prior as a single discovery. The update factors are deliberately moderate for external honors because awards are correlated and their timing relative to a Nobel is uncertain.

| Discovery | Starting probability | Update factor | Final unnormalized weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Topological insulators/QSH | 0.150 | 1.00 | 0.15000 |
| Optical lattice clocks | 0.150 | 1.40 | 0.21000 |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 0.050 | 1.00 | 0.05000 |
| Geometric phases | 0.060 | 1.00 | 0.06000 |
| Magic-angle graphene | 0.045 | 1.85 | 0.08325 |
| Foundational quantum information | 0.080 | 1.25 | 0.10000 |
| Cosmic neutrinos | 0.040 | 1.00 | 0.04000 |
| Black-hole shadow | 0.030 | 1.00 | 0.03000 |
| Optical-lattice quantum simulation | 0.055 | 1.65 | 0.09075 |
| Quantum cascade laser | 0.045 | 1.00 | 0.04500 |
| Aberration-corrected electron optics | 0.055 | 1.00 | 0.05500 |
| Inflation | 0.015 | 1.00 | 0.01500 |
| Other | 0.225 | 2.25 | 0.50625 |

The clocks factor combines continued institutional progress with a discounted Wolf signal. The simulation factor reflects the specific Bloch recognition. Graphene’s larger proportional update reflects the direct 2026 Kavli recognition of a category with a relatively low starting probability. Quantum information receives a smaller uplift for the verified Turing announcement. Other’s update reflects the independently checked OLED, multiferroic, and Galactic-assembly omissions, QAH classification uncertainty, and a remaining tail of discoveries not captured by this list.

I calculated the normalized probabilities in Python:

**P(i) = starting_probability(i) × update_factor(i) / 1.43525.**

For example, clocks receive 0.21000 / 1.43525 = 0.146315973, and Other receives 0.50625 / 1.43525 ≈ 0.352726006. The final object uses nine decimal places, with Other adjusted in the last decimal place so the reported numbers sum exactly to 1. These inputs expose where judgment enters: another analyst can reproduce the arithmetic exactly, while reasonably disagreeing with the starting probabilities or update factors.

Clarivate itself cautions that its recognition does not predict recipients in a particular Nobel year; I use it to identify credible omissions, not as an annual forecast aggregate. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/?utm_source=openai))

Independent prize records add other omissions: the 2026 Kavli Astrophysics Prize recognized evidence of the Milky Way's hierarchical assembly; the April 18, 2026 Breakthrough announcement recognized muon magnetic-moment measurements; and the 2016 Kavli Nanoscience Prize recognized atomic force microscopy. Each supplies a scientifically credible, unlisted route, although none individually establishes Nobel intent. This wider pool motivates increasing Other's structural weight by **1.90**. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2026))

## 5. Resolution-boundary handling

I do not equate related scientific labels automatically. A motivation specifically rewarding **quantum anomalous Hall realization** may resolve Other rather than quantum spin Hall/topological insulators: QAH involves broken time-reversal symmetry, whereas the Kane–Mele QSH state is time-reversal invariant. A broader motivation explicitly rewarding discovery of topological insulators could instead match the listed option. I retain uncertainty over that boundary rather than assigning all Xue-related probability to either side. ([journals.aps.org](https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.95.011002))

Similarly, an award for photonic band gaps alone is not automatically negative-index metamaterials, and a prize for trapped-ion computing alone is not automatically neutral-atom optical-lattice simulation. Conversely, twistronics recognition centered on the listed correlated states and superconductivity should not become Other merely because the wording or laureate names differ. These boundary risks are included in the overall Other allocation rather than added as independent probabilities after normalization.

## 6. Reproducible probability calculation

I used a **judgmental normalized-weight model**, not a statistically fitted classifier. The baseline weights sum to 100 and summarize the older scientific/award record and structural suitability. The multipliers summarize the additional evidence and selection considerations discussed above. They are **not empirically estimated likelihood ratios**. Reproducing the arithmetic reproduces my estimate; the subjective weights remain open to disagreement.

| Discovery | Baseline weight | Multiplier | Final unnormalized weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Topological insulators / QSH | 15 | 1.00 | 15.00 |
| Optical lattice clocks | 16 | 1.25 | 20.00 |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 6 | 1.00 | 6.00 |
| Geometric phases | 6 | 1.00 | 6.00 |
| Magic-angle graphene | 4 | 1.80 | 7.20 |
| Quantum-information foundations | 7 | 0.80 | 5.60 |
| High-energy cosmic neutrinos | 4 | 1.30 | 5.20 |
| Black-hole shadow | 3 | 0.90 | 2.70 |
| Optical-lattice quantum simulation | 6 | 0.85 | 5.10 |
| Quantum cascade laser | 4 | 1.00 | 4.00 |
| Aberration-corrected electron optics | 7 | 1.10 | 7.70 |
| Cosmic inflation | 1 | 0.70 | 0.70 |
| Other | 21 | 1.90 | 39.90 |

The denominator is **125.10**. For each category, `probability = final unnormalized weight / 125.10`. I performed the calculations with decimal arithmetic in Python, rounded to six decimal places, and assigned the negligible rounding residual to Other so the reported probabilities sum exactly to 1.000000.

## 7. Uncertainty and limitations

The extra decimal places preserve the calculation; they do **not** imply knowledge of Nobel voting to that precision. To test dependence on my largest judgments, I varied the clock multiplier from 0.80 to 1.80 and the Other multiplier from 1.30 to 2.70, holding other weights fixed. Across the four corner scenarios, clocks range from **9.5% to 23.7%**, topological insulators from **10.0% to 14.2%**, and Other from **22.5% to 42.1%**. These are sensitivity scenarios, not statistical confidence intervals. Uncertainty in the other weights would widen them further.

The largest remaining unknown is confidential committee preference, followed by the interpretation of broad or divided motivations. Some official pages blocked direct retrieval, so I cross-checked their indexed official text and historical records; I did not treat a failed fetch or absence from search results as proof that an event had not occurred. The final distribution deliberately avoids a dominant named favorite and retains substantial probability for credible omissions and unexpected choices.

## TL;DR
My forecast assigns 36.5% to Other, the largest category. Optical lattice clocks lead the named options at 15%, followed by topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect at 10%. Fresh awards establish scientific standing; they do not identify the confidential Nobel choice ([selection process](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/)).

## Context
This forecast uses information available by October 2, 2026, at 14:29 UTC. The Physics announcement is scheduled for October 6, no earlier than 11:45 CEST, or 09:45 UTC ([official schedule](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/)). The committee prepares recommendations over summer and submits them in September; the Academy makes its final selection in early October. Nominations and assessments remain confidential for 50 years ([official process](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/)). This is therefore a forecast of a hidden institutional choice. No post-cutoff result, prediction-market price, or public forecast aggregate enters the estimate.

## Evidence
The historical backbone argues against turning a fresh precursor award into a large timing signal. I audited the complete 2010–2020 Wolf Physics cohorts against Physics Nobel outcomes through 2025, using historical records available at the cutoff. The sample contains 19 individuals across nine awarded years. Every cohort has complete follow-up for award-year lag zero through five ([Wolf records](https://wolffund.org.il/anton-zeilinger/), [Nobel records](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-prizes-in-physics/all/)).

| [2011](https://wolffund.org.il/maximilian-haider/) | Haider, Rose, Urban | None |
| [2012](https://wolffund.org.il/jacob-bekenstein/) | Bekenstein | None |
| [2013](https://wolffund.org.il/juan-ignacio-cirac/) | Cirac, Zoller | None |
| [2014](https://wolffund.org.il/category/field/physics/) | No Physics recipients listed | Not applicable |

| [2016](https://wolffund.org.il/imry-yoseph/) | Imry | None |
| [2017](https://wolffund.org.il/didier-queloz/) | Mayor, Queloz | Both in [2019](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2019/summary/), at lag 2 |

That is two of 19 individuals, or 11%, within the specified window, and zero same-calendar-year conversions. But the two successes represent one shared discovery and one Nobel decision. Splitting the separately cited contributions in the 2015 Wolf award gives ten discovery themes, only one of which converted within the window ([Wolf citations](https://wolffund.org.il/james-d-bjorken/), [Nobel outcome](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2019/summary/)). This small, clustered sample is a check on publicity-driven enthusiasm, not a direct probability estimate for any candidate. It counts receipt of any Nobel share, not necessarily the discovery that would control this question's resolution.

Optical lattice clocks have the strongest named case. Their invention and development received a closely matching 2022 Breakthrough citation, announced on September 9, 2021 ([award announcement](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/65)). The Wolf Foundation's September 30, 2026 announcement jointly recognizes Ye and Bloch for ultracold-atom control, explicitly connecting Ye to clocks and Bloch to quantum simulation ([2026 Wolf announcement](https://wolffund.org.il/home-page/)). I give both options a positive update, but not an independent, large bonus for every overlapping award. The metrological importance is concrete: BIPM's FAQ, updated March 21, 2025, says optical standards have surpassed caesium standards, while putting ratification of a redefined second no earlier than 2030 ([BIPM roadmap](https://www.bipm.org/en/faq-redefinition-second)). The redefinition is a future milestone, not a completed trigger for this year's Nobel.

Topological insulators remain a strong runner-up. The experimental QSH result and the independently recognized theoretical framework form a mature theory-to-experiment package ([HgTe experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.0582), [Breakthrough citation](https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/L3829)). The earlier Nobel for topological phases creates a real overlap discount, but it does not mean this later discovery has already been awarded ([2016 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2016/summary/)). I likewise treat the neighboring quantum-information and circuit awards as modest comparative headwinds, not a field-rotation veto ([2022 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2022/summary/), [2025 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2025/summary/)).

Metamaterials have a genuine institutional-attention signal. Umeå hosted the symposium on June 29–July 1, 2026; its organizer confirms Nobel Committee participation, and Wilczek's participant account reports that the entire Physics Committee attended alongside speakers including Pendry and Smith ([organizer's September account](https://ucmrblogg.umu.se/when-the-world-of-metamaterials-came-to-umea-a-story-of-shared-curiosity/), [participant account](https://www.frankawilczek.com/single-post/frank-wilczek-at-the-2026-nobel-symposium-in-physics)). I raise the negative-index option on that evidence. The update stays restrained because the meeting was publicly announced in November 2025 and covered a much broader field than negative refraction ([advance announcement](https://www.umu.se/en/news/two-nobel-symposia-at-umea-university-in-2026_12148986/)).

Other is not just a surprise reserve. Clarivate's September 17, 2026 recognition identifies efficient OLEDs, magnetoelectric multiferroics, and the quantum anomalous Hall effect—credible research packages outside, or at the boundary of, the supplied options. Clarivate itself says its program does not predict recipients in a particular year ([dated announcement and citations](https://ir.clarivate.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Clarivate-Reveals-Citation-Laureates-2026-Recognizing-Transformative-Scientific-Breakthroughs/default.aspx)). The later fractional-quantum-Hall and composite-fermion achievements recognized by the 2025 Wolf Prize add another substantial omitted competitor ([Wolf citation](https://wolffund.org.il/jainendra-k-jain/)). These examples establish incomplete coverage; they do not supply an empirical coverage percentage.

My numerical construction separates omitted-discovery risk from the relative strength of named outcomes. The following are judgmental inputs, not fitted committee preferences. I use three coverage scenarios: Other receives 25%, 36.0%, or 49.0%, with weights of one-quarter, one-half, and one-quarter. Their weighted mean is 36.5%. This already includes nearby discoveries whose official motivation would fail to match a listed option.

I distribute the remaining probability using the following dimensionless scores. They incorporate maturity, confirmation, recognition, overlap, credit allocation, and discovery specificity.

| Named discovery | Score | Main assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| Optical lattice clocks | 26 | Clean, mature measurement achievement with a closely matching [major-prize citation](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/65). |
| Topological insulators/QSH | 17 | Strong theory–experiment chain; discounted for [earlier topology recognition](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2016/summary/). |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 11 | Mature achievement, reinforced by [Pendry's Kyoto citation](https://www.kyotoprize.org/en/laureates/john_pendry/) and committee exposure. |
| Magic-angle graphene | 10 | The [2026 Kavli citation](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/nanoscience/2026) strongly reinforces twistronics and its correlated-state results; the central experimental discovery is comparatively young. |
| Geometric/topological quantum phases | 9 | Foundational, established work with fresh [2026 Wigner recognition](https://wignermedal.tamu.edu/). |
| Optical-lattice quantum simulators | 9 | Direct platform-specific validation from the [2025 Micius award](https://www.mpq.mpg.de/7090895/08-micius-quantum-prize-for-immanuel-bloch), plus the new Wolf recognition. |
| Quantum-information foundations | 8 | Strong merit signal from the Turing award announced March 18, 2026; neighboring Nobels limit the update ([dated recognition](https://www.nsf.gov/cise/updates/pioneers-quantum-information-science-recognized-2025-acm-am)). |
| High-energy cosmic neutrinos | 6 | A confirmed observational advance with directly relevant [APS recognition](https://www.aps.org/apsnews/2025/12/medal-francis-halzen). |
| Aberration-corrected electron optics | 6 | Mature, transformative instrumentation; individual credit remains complicated by the [four-person Kavli package](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/nanoscience/2020). |
| Quantum cascade laser | 4 | A specific, long-matured device invention competing with stronger instrumentation candidates ([original paper](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2883703)). |
| Black-hole shadow | 3 | Major observation, but comparatively recent and close to already honored black-hole science ([EHT announcement](https://eventhorizontelescope.org/press-release-april-10-2019-astronomers-capture-first-image-black-hole), [2020 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2020/summary/)). |
| Cosmic inflation | 1.5 | Foundational importance, but a less direct confirmation story; recent observational work still describes primordial-wave detection as a future goal ([September 2026 research account](https://news.uchicago.edu/story/south-pole-telescope-releases-clearest-map-ever-matter-distant-universe)). |

The scores sum to 110.5. For each named outcome I calculate \(p_i=(1-p_O)s_i/\sum_j s_j\), where \(p_O\) is the Other probability and \(s_i\) is its score. The delivered values are normalized to sum exactly to one.

## What's non-obvious
The IceCube event at the Nobel Prize Museum looks like an insider signal until its scheduling history is checked. The October 6 evening talk was already specified in a Stockholm University notice published in April and updated May 12, months before the final selection, as part of ordinary Nobel Calling outreach ([advance planning notice](https://medarbetare.su.se/vart-su/medarbetarinformation/nyheter-for-medarbetare/nyhetsarkiv/2026-04-28-anmal-evenemang-till-nobel-calling-i-oktober)). Its advertised speakers are Finley and Lidström, and its subject is general IceCube research and work at the South Pole ([event listing](https://www.nobelprizemuseum.se/nobel-calling-stockholm/aktiviteter/jakten-pa-neutriner-i-sydpolens-is/)). I remove any special scheduling bonus. Halzen's APS recognition still counts as evidence of merit.

Discovery matching cuts both ways. Different recipients do not invalidate a match, but related subjects do not automatically qualify. A QAH-only motivation would fall under Other in my central interpretation, whereas a broader topological-insulator motivation could match the listed option ([recognized QAH discovery](https://ir.clarivate.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Clarivate-Reveals-Citation-Laureates-2026-Recognizing-Transformative-Scientific-Breakthroughs/default.aspx)). Similarly, optical clocks are not synonymous with optical lattice clocks: NIST's July 14, 2025 accuracy-record announcement concerned an ion clock ([NIST announcement](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/07/nist-ion-clock-sets-new-record-most-accurate-clock-world)). Broad quantum or photonics enthusiasm therefore supports less probability for these narrowly specified options than it first appears to.

## Uncertainties
The largest gaps are the confidential candidate set, the committee's comparative scientific assessments, and the eventual wording of the motivation ([confidentiality rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/)). A reliable shortlist or assessment would matter more than another public honor. The precursor sample is small and clustered; zero same-year conversions in that window does not establish impossibility. Public awards also share a common signal of scientific standing, so they cannot be treated as independent evidence.

The model's largest assumption is shortlist coverage. Holding named scores fixed, changing Other from 25% to 49.0% moves clocks from 18% to 12% and topological insulators from 12% to 8%. These are assumption-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals. The extra JSON digits preserve the calculation and normalization; they do not represent six-decimal knowledge of the Academy's choice.

## Forecast

My modal outcome is **Other (42.0%)**. Among the named discoveries, I rank **optical lattice clocks (10.2%)**, **negative-index metamaterials (8.1%)**, and **magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (7.9%)** highest. The Nobel Prize in Physics is scheduled for announcement on **Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 11:45 CEST at the earliest**. This forecast uses information available by **October 2, 2026, 14:05 UTC** and no post-announcement information. ([somo.social](https://somo.social/e/jakten-pa-neutriner-i-sydpolens-is-6-oktober-2026?utm_source=openai))

## Method

I used a structured, semi-quantitative model with six considerations:

1. **Scientific importance and confirmation:** Is the discovery broadly accepted and experimentally established?
2. **Maturity:** Nobel Physics usually rewards work after its importance has survived substantial scrutiny, although unusually fast awards sometimes occur.
3. **Attribution fit:** Can the Academy defend selecting no more than three living individuals? The question resolves by discovery rather than exact laureates, but contested attribution still reduces the probability that the discovery itself is selected.
4. **Precursor recognition:** Wolf, Kavli, Breakthrough, Kyoto, APS and comparable awards.
5. **Field rotation and overlap:** Recent Physics prizes reduce, but do not eliminate, the probability of another closely related award.
6. **2026 weak signals:** Recent awards, Swedish events, symposium topics, standards activity and current specialist commentary. I treated these as small updates rather than leaks.

Nobel nominations and deliberations are confidential for 50 years, so public candidate lists cannot reveal the actual shortlist. ([nobelprizemuseum.se](https://www.nobelprizemuseum.se/en/nobel-calling-stockholm/?utm_source=openai))

I first formed an independent forecast from scientific and historical evidence. I did not use prediction-market prices in constructing the estimate. No sufficiently useful liquid market or Metaculus aggregate for this exact question was found during the subsequent sanity check.

## Base rates and the `Other` probability

The supplied list is broad, but it still omits several credible 2026 candidates. Clarivate’s current Physics Citation Laureates concern ultrahigh-efficiency OLEDs, magnetoelectric multiferroics and the quantum anomalous Hall effect—all `Other` under these resolution rules. Physics World additionally discussed antihydrogen, quark-gluon plasma and wavelet theory, while also highlighting several listed discoveries. This makes a large residual essential. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014?utm_source=openai))

I therefore assign **42% to Other**. This is not a claim that one omitted discovery is clearly leading; it represents the combined probability of many omitted candidates plus genuine Nobel surprise risk.

I also matched the Wolf Foundation’s 72 Physics laureates through 2025 against NobelPrize.org’s Physics laureates. Twenty-six of 72, or **36.1%**, had received a Physics Nobel by the end of 2025. Only four individuals—three Wolf award-year episodes—won in the same calendar year, corresponding to **5.6% of individuals** or **8.3% of award-year episodes**. Thus the September 30 announcement of the 2026 Wolf Prize to Jun Ye and Immanuel Bloch is meaningful evidence of Nobel-level standing, but historically it points more strongly to eventual recognition than specifically to a Nobel four days later. The underlying records came from the Wolf archive and Nobel’s official laureate data. 

## 2026-specific weak signals

Several options received unusually timely recognition:

- **Jun Ye and Immanuel Bloch** received the 2026 Wolf Physics Prize for control of ultracold atomic systems—Ye for optical clocks and Bloch for quantum simulation. 
- **Eva Andrei, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Allan MacDonald** received the 2026 Kavli Nanoscience Prize for foundational work establishing twistronics. 
- **Michael Berry and Yakir Aharonov** received the 2026 Wigner Medal for foundational discoveries in quantum mechanics. ([kva.se](https://www.kva.se/en/news/autumn-nobel-announcements-confirmed-3/?utm_source=openai))
- **Francis Halzen** received the 2026 APS Medal for IceCube and high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. In addition, the Nobel Prize Museum scheduled an IceCube neutrino-astronomy event for the evening of October 6. The event is a genuine but highly speculative signal because it is part of a broad public festival containing many unrelated activities. ([kavlifoundation.org](https://www.kavlifoundation.org/news/2014-kavli-prize-astrophysics-discussion-alan-guth-andrei-linde-and-alexei?utm_source=openai))
- A 2026 Nobel Symposium in Umeå focused on metamaterials and included leading pioneers plus observers from the Academy and Physics Nobel Committee. This indicates active Academy-level evaluation of the field, but Nobel Symposia often precede relevant prizes by years rather than months. 
- Bennett and Brassard received the 2025 ACM Turing Award, announced in March 2026, for foundational quantum-information work. 

These signals are correlated: elite prize committees often recognize the same mature fields. I therefore did not simply add a large bonus for every 2026 award.

## Option-by-option assessment

### Optical lattice clocks — 10.2%

This is my leading named option. Katori proposed the optical-lattice-clock concept in the early 2000s, and Katori and Ye shared the 2022 Breakthrough Prize for its invention and development. The attribution is exceptionally clean, the technology is experimentally mature, and discussions about redefining the SI second give it a timely public narrative. Ye’s 2026 Wolf Prize adds another strong precursor signal. The main negative is rotation: the 2022 and 2025 prizes already rewarded quantum-information experiments and macroscopic quantum circuits, respectively. ([hhs.se](https://www.hhs.se/events/gapp/2026/nobel-calling-when-crises-meet-digital-payments/?utm_source=openai))

### Negative-index metamaterials — 8.1%

Metamaterials have roughly a quarter-century of maturity, and Pendry’s theoretical role is exceptionally well established. His 2024 Kyoto Prize, the 2026 Nobel Symposium, current Swedish commentary and Physics World’s 2026 discussion create a notable cluster of weak signals. The disadvantages are diffuse attribution—Smith, Engheta, Capasso, Alù and others have plausible claims—and uncertainty over whether the Academy sees negative refraction itself, broader metamaterials, or metasurfaces as the prizeworthy discovery. ([nobelprizemuseum.se](https://www.nobelprizemuseum.se/en/nobel-calling-stockholm/activities/the-hunt-for-neutrinos-at-the-south-pole/?utm_source=openai))

### Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene — 7.9%

This has perhaps the strongest fresh precursor award: the 2026 Kavli Prize for twistronics. The theoretical magic-angle prediction dates to 2011 and the decisive correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments to 2018. The theory–experiment story is highly Nobel-like, and the field is scientifically prominent. I keep it below clocks because eight years since the signature experiment is fast by Nobel standards, and the microscopic interpretation of the superconductivity remains debated. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014?utm_source=openai))

### High-energy cosmic neutrinos — 6.4%

Halzen’s 2026 APS Medal directly recognizes IceCube’s discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and their sources. The same-day Nobel Museum event is an intriguing but weak scheduling anomaly. IceCube has established a new observational channel, and Nobel has previously rewarded leaders of large observatories. The negatives are attribution across a large collaboration and earlier neutrino prizes in 2002 and 2015. ([kavlifoundation.org](https://www.kavlifoundation.org/news/2014-kavli-prize-astrophysics-discussion-alan-guth-andrei-linde-and-alexei?utm_source=openai))

### Quantum simulators using ultracold atoms — 5.1%

Bloch, Cirac and Zoller provide a coherent theory–experiment narrative, and the field is mature. Bloch’s 2026 Wolf Prize and Cirac’s inaugural 2026 Richard Feynman Prize are strong evidence of current standing. However, experimental credit also extends to Greiner, Esslinger and others, while another quantum-technology prize immediately after 2025 would be somewhat repetitive. 

### Aberration-corrected electron optics — 4.4%

This is an archetypal Nobel instrumentation achievement: mature, widely adopted and transformative across materials science. It has strong Wolf and Kavli precursor recognition. Its largest problem is the three-person cap: the 2020 Kavli Prize identified four central contributors—Harald Rose, Haider, Urban and Krivanek—with Rose supplying the foundational corrector design. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/alan-guth-autobiography?utm_source=openai))

### Geometric and topological phases — 4.1%

Berry and Aharonov have an unusually clean two-person story, shared the 1998 Wolf Prize, and received the 2026 Wigner Medal. Their discoveries have influenced many areas of physics. The probability is limited because the work has remained unrewarded by Nobel for decades, the Aharonov–Bohm and Berry phases are historically distinct discoveries, and the 2016 topology prize creates some conceptual overlap. ([kth.se](https://www.kth.se/en/2.844/kalender/nobel-calling-open-lecture-robotik-ai-och-manniskan-utmaningar-och-mojligheter-1.1488573?date=2026-10-07&length=1&orgdate=2026-04-09&orglength=267&utm_source=openai))

### Quantum cascade laser — 3.4%

The QCL is mature, technologically important and specific enough for a clear invention-based citation. Capasso was singled out in Physics World’s current discussion. But the original 1994 demonstration had six prominent contributors, making any three-person selection contentious, and lasers received a major Physics prize as recently as 2018. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014?utm_source=openai))

### Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect — 2.6%

The work is mature and has a compelling theory–experiment chain, with Kane and Mele receiving the Breakthrough Prize. Nevertheless, the 2016 Nobel explicitly rewarded topological phases of matter, and Shoucheng Zhang’s central but now posthumously ineligible role complicates the canonical laureate grouping. Current Clarivate attention to Qikun Xue concerns the distinct quantum anomalous Hall effect and would resolve as `Other`, not this option. ([nobelprizemuseum.se](https://www.nobelprizemuseum.se/en/nobel-calling-stockholm/?utm_source=openai))

### Foundational quantum information — 2.4%

The scientific importance is unquestioned, and the 2026 Turing recognition of Bennett and Brassard is timely. But a broad prize combining quantum cryptography and algorithms has attribution problems—Deutsch is another obvious foundational figure—and the 2022 Nobel motivation already explicitly included pioneering quantum information science. The 2025 circuit prize further strengthens the rotation penalty. ([gcn.nasa.gov](https://gcn.nasa.gov/missions/icecube?utm_source=openai))

### Cosmic inflation — 1.9%

Inflation is foundational and has extensive precursor recognition, including the 2014 Kavli Prize to Guth, Linde and Starobinsky and the Gruber Prize to Mukhanov and Starobinsky. However, Starobinsky is deceased, the supplied trio is not the uniquely canonical attribution, and no primordial gravitational-wave signature has yet been detected; BICEP/Keck instead supplies an upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014?utm_source=openai))

### Black-hole shadow — 1.5%

The EHT image is iconic and clearly important, but it is only seven years old, selecting three people from the collaboration would be controversial, and the 2020 Physics Nobel already focused on black holes. Current next-generation EHT funding is better interpreted as evidence that the observational program remains in active development than as a Nobel-specific signal. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014?utm_source=openai))

## Calibration and main uncertainties

The central uncertainty is not which listed candidate is strongest, but whether the eventual motivation is represented at all. A condensed-matter or materials prize looks somewhat more likely than usual, yet the strongest current formal candidate signal—Clarivate’s slate—is entirely in `Other`. Conversely, multiple independent signals favor clocks, metamaterials, twistronics and IceCube.

I deliberately keep the leading named option near 10%, rather than assigning 15–20%, because Nobel Physics predictions have a poor record of identifying the correct year even when they identify eventual laureates. The 2026 Wolf, Kavli, APS, Wigner and Turing awards mainly establish Nobel-level merit; they provide much less information about the Academy’s exact October 2026 choice.

## Forecast summary

**Other is my most likely individual outcome, at 31.4107%. Optical lattice clocks are my leading named discovery, at 19.2887%, followed by topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, at 11.5403%.** The remaining probability is distributed across several credible alternatives rather than concentrated in one presumed runner-up.

These are judgmental probabilities informed by scientific maturity, major independent recognition, previous Nobel motivations, and the question’s discovery-matching rules. They are not estimates derived from knowledge of the confidential Nobel shortlist. ## 1. Forecast cutoff and interpretation

I use **October 2, 2026, 14:05 UTC** as the information cutoff. The official schedule places the Physics announcement on **October 6, 2026, at 11:45 CEST at the earliest**, equivalent to **09:45 UTC**. That is 91 hours and 40 minutes after the cutoff. This remains a genuinely prospective forecast, not an attempt to identify an already announced winner. 

I follow the supplied resolution criteria in three important ways:

1. **Discovery, not the exact laureate combination, determines the outcome.** A prize involving David Deutsch could still match the quantum-information option. A magic-angle graphene prize involving Eva Andrei instead of Rafi Bistritzer could still match the graphene option.
2. **For a divided prize, only the larger-share discovery counts; equal shares are resolved by announcement order.** I therefore estimate the discovery that controls resolution, not the probability that a discovery appears anywhere in the announcement.
3. **Related scientific subjects are not automatically identical discoveries.** A prize specifically for photonic crystals, metalenses, trapped-ion quantum computing, or the quantum anomalous Hall effect would not necessarily match negative-index metamaterials, optical-lattice quantum simulation, or quantum spin Hall discovery.

The official selection process makes direct candidate inference difficult: nominations are confidential for 50 years, nominations normally close on January 31, expert consultation occurs during spring, recommendations are prepared over summer and considered in September, and the Academy makes its final selection in October. Thus, external prizes are evidence of scientific standing—not evidence of Nobel nomination, committee preference, or a causal influence on this year’s choice.

## 5. Reproducible numerical construction

I used a subjective weighted-hypothesis model. **The starting weights and evidence multipliers below are judgmental inputs, not fitted coefficients or statistically measured likelihood ratios.** The model makes those judgments inspectable rather than hiding them behind a precise final number.

The starting weights reflect maturity, importance, independent recognition preceding the newer updates, previous Nobel overlap, and the breadth of omitted physics. The new-evidence multipliers then give moderate additional weight to the verified 2026 recognition. Because external prizes are correlated indicators of scientific standing, I deliberately avoid enormous multipliers.

| Programme | Starting weight b | Evidence multiplier u | Discovery-match fraction m |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Topological insulators/QSH | 0.140 | 1.00 | 0.97 |
| Optical lattice clocks | 0.180 | 1.30 | 0.97 |
| Negative-index metamaterials | 0.060 | 1.00 | 0.90 |
| Geometric phases | 0.035 | 1.00 | 0.98 |
| Magic-angle graphene | 0.040 | 1.60 | 0.96 |
| Quantum information | 0.065 | 1.15 | 0.98 |
| Cosmic neutrinos | 0.040 | 1.00 | 0.98 |
| Black-hole shadow | 0.030 | 1.00 | 0.99 |
| Ultracold-lattice simulation | 0.040 | 1.80 | 0.95 |
| Quantum cascade laser | 0.025 | 1.00 | 0.99 |
| Electron microscopy | 0.050 | 1.00 | 0.99 |
| Cosmic inflation | 0.010 | 1.00 | 0.98 |
| Other | 0.285 | 1.20 | 1.00 |

The match fractions represent the small portion of a **broader programme-level hypothesis** that could instead produce a motivation for a neighboring, unlisted discovery. They do not penalize alternative laureate names. The explicit shares/order rule is incorporated by interpreting the programme hypothesis as the contribution controlling resolution, not simply any contribution receiving a share.

I calculated in Python:

- Raw weights: wᵢ = bᵢ × uᵢ.
- Normalization constant: Z = Σwᵢ = **1.17675**.
- Programme probabilities: qᵢ = wᵢ/Z.
- Named-option probabilities: pᵢ = qᵢ × mᵢ.
- Other: pOther = qOther + Σ[qᵢ × (1−mᵢ)] over the named programmes.

Before discovery matching, Other is **0.2906309751**. The matching adjustment transfers **0.0234756745** to Other, giving **0.3141066497** before output rounding. Optical lattice clocks finish at approximately **0.1928871893**. I rounded the complete vector to six decimal places using largest-remainder rounding so that the reported values sum exactly to **1.000000**.

## 1. Resolution interpretation and institutional constraints

I forecast the **discovery selected by the official motivation**, not the exact laureate slate. Consequently, a prize for optical lattice clocks can resolve to that option even if someone other than the two listed scientists shares it. Likewise, attribution disagreements concerning the listed third person do not themselves invalidate the metamaterials, microscopy, neutrino, or black-hole-shadow options.

For a divided prize, I apply the question's rule to the combined share associated with each discovery: the larger discovery share wins; an equal-share tie is settled by announcement order. My probability model concerns the primary discovery *after* those rules are applied. It does not count every discovery mentioned in a divided award as a separate YES.

The Nobel process is unusually opaque. The official process description states that nominations and deliberations remain confidential for 50 years; nominations close on 31 January; expert assessment follows in spring; recommendations are prepared during summer and submitted in September; the Academy makes the final selection in early October. Thus, publicity in the last few days is not evidence of a newly submitted nomination, and absence from public commentary is not evidence of absence from consideration. My inference is that, this close to announcement, the main uncertainty is hidden selection information rather than a new scientific result arriving in the remaining days. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/?utm_source=openai))

I pursued four particularly decision-relevant research threads: **whether recent recognition materially strengthens clocks and quantum simulation; whether the 2026 quantum-anomalous-Hall recognition belongs in the topological-insulator option; how strong the unlisted opportunity set is; and whether precursor-prize history justifies a large near-term probability boost.**
